subject: Post-demo: Inference acceptance criteria, harness onboarding & next steps
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Sandeep Rao <sandeep@finlytics.ai>
Cc: Elena Morales <elena.morales@finlytics.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-12-20T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Post-demo: Inference acceptance criteria, harness onboarding & next steps

Hi Sandeep / Elena — thanks again for your time this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment before we kick off the performance qualification: 

Summary of requirements you confirmed:
- Latency SLO: 95th percentile < 220ms for 256-token completions (interactive search use-case).
- Throughput target: sustained 300 qps for 2k concurrent users during peak (model concurrency target per GPU TBD).
- Streaming: token-level streaming required for progressive UI render; max initial chunk latency 80ms.
- KV cache expectations: customer will send session IDs and expect warm-cache hit-rate > 60% for returning users.

What we are attaching here:
- slo_acceptance_matrix.xlsx — proposed measurement buckets (p50/p95/p99, steady-state windows, error thresholds).
- eval_harness_onboarding.md — step-by-step to stand up the harness in your GCP project (runner, load generator, dataset mounts).
- sample_prompt_bundle.jsonl — 200 anonymized prompts representative of your search queries for the qualification run.

Proposed next steps (timeline):
1) You confirm the acceptance matrix and mark any missing buckets by Tue 12/22.
2) Finlytics grants Redwood a short-term binding-read-only service account in the test project by 12/23 so we can run the harness.
3) Redwood will run a validation run (non-production) and share raw metrics and reproducibility instructions by 12/30.
4) Joint tuning session week of 1/5 to iterate batching/quantization recommendations.

Ask: please confirm the acceptance criteria in the spreadsheet and who on your side will own the IAM grant for the test harness.

Thanks,
Ben
Ben Carter | Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0198
Redwood Inference

Attachments: slo_acceptance_matrix.xlsx (spreadsheet), eval_harness_onboarding.md (text), sample_prompt_bundle.jsonl (JSONL)

From: Sandeep Rao <sandeep@finlytics.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Elena Morales <elena.morales@finlytics.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-12-20T11:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: Inference acceptance criteria, harness onboarding & next steps

Ben — thanks for the clear recap. Elena and I reviewed the spreadsheet and it looks good overall. A couple of clarifications before we confirm: 

1) The 300 qps number is for sustained queries across our primary index; during promotions we may need to burst to 450 qps for short windows (~5 minutes). Can you accommodate a defined burst profile without violating the SLOs?
2) For streaming, we want client-side partial rendering at token boundaries. Is the harness able to measure chunk-level latency and provide sample traces we can pipe into our UI team?
3) On IAM: I will loop in our platform engineer (cc'd private) and we can create a service account with read-only access to the test index and an ability to call Redwood-hosted inference endpoints. ETA for the grant: 12/23 EOD.

If Redwood can include the burst profile and provide chunk-level streaming traces in the validation report, we can sign off quickly.

— Sandeep
Sandeep Rao | Head of Product, Finlytics.ai

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Sandeep Rao <sandeep@finlytics.ai>
Cc: Elena Morales <elena.morales@finlytics.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-12-21T08:30:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: Inference acceptance criteria, harness onboarding & next steps

Sandeep — great questions. Short answers inline below and plan of action: 

1) Burst profile: yes — we can emulate the 450 qps 5-minute burst and will include burst windows in the acceptance matrix (added a "burst" column in the attached spreadsheet). We will run both steady-state and burst scenarios and report separate SLO compliance numbers.

2) Chunk-level traces: the harness collects per-chunk send/recv timestamps and will produce trace snippets (HAR-like) you can feed into your UI/telemetry. We'll attach a sample trace in the validation report.

3) IAM logistics: thanks — once your platform engineer creates the service account we will provide an onboarding checklist (minimal permissions only).

Timeline update: given your EOD 12/23 for IAM, we will target the validation run for 12/28 and delivery of raw metrics + trace artifacts by 12/30. If we need earlier, we can prioritize but we'd want confirmation of the service account earlier in the day on 12/23.

Internal note (below) — planning: Marcus will own the harness run and coordinate the runner configuration; Laura will handle the measurement review and draft the validation report.

Thanks,
Ben

--- Original internal note ---
From: Ben Carter
To: Laura Bennett, Marcus Lin
Date: 2026-12-21T08:32:00-08:00

Laura / Marcus — please see the customer asks (burst window + chunk traces). Action items for us:
- Marcus: prepare runner config with burst profile (450 qps, 5m) and steady-state 300 qps sustained for 30m. Bring quantization profile candidates (q4_0, q4_k_mixed) for tuning.
- Laura: update the acceptance matrix with separate steady-state and burst pass/fail columns; include chunk-latency pass thresholds (initial chunk < 80ms, subsequent chunk p95 < 120ms).
- Both: tag all results with a reproducibility ID and include the exact harness commit hash in the report.

Ben

From: Elena Morales <elena.morales@finlytics.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sandeep Rao <sandeep@finlytics.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-12-23T15:20:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: Inference acceptance criteria, harness onboarding & next steps

Thanks — confirmed from our side: IAM grant will be created today (12/23) and you should have the service account by 18:00 PST. We appreciate the inclusion of burst windows and chunk traces. A couple of additional asks: 

- Can the harness encrypt traces at rest? We'll need them to be protected while staging.
- Please include an appendix in the validation report describing any model variants or quantization settings you tested (so our compliance team can review).

If you can meet the 12/28 validation run target, we will prepare acceptance sign-off by 1/7 after reviewing the validation report. Looking forward to the harness run.

Best,
Elena
Elena Morales | VP Engineering, Finlytics.ai
